semantic_fragments.content:
Condition of acceptability:
1) 201.11.7 Biocompatibility of ME EQUIPMENT and ME is not evaluated in this report.
2) 201.17 Electromagnetic compatibility of ME EQUIPMENT and ME SYSTEMS is not evaluated in this report.
3) 201.102 CLINICAL ACCURACY VALIDATION is not evaluated in this report.
4) 202 Electromagnetic disturbances - Requirements and tests is not evaluated in this report.
5) 206 Usability is not evaluated in this report.

The tests results presented in this report relate only to the object tested. This report shall not be reproduced except in full without the written approval of the testing laboratory. List of test equipment must be kept on file and available for review. This Test Report Form is intended for the investigation of clinical thermometers for body temperature measurement in accordance with EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017/A1:2020/ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018. It can only be used together with IEC 60601-1:2005. Additional test data and/or information provided in the attachments to this report. Throughout this report a comma/point is used as the decimal separator.
The artwork below may be only a draft. The use of certification marks on a product must be authorized by the respective NCBs that own these marks.

The packaging of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER and PROBE is marked with: a) MEASURING SITE and REFERENCE BODY SITE (N/A); b) mode of operation of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER; c) appropriate symbol from ISO 15223-1:2016 for sterile packaging (Table 201.D.2.101, symbols 3-8); d) Symbol 5.1.4 of ISO 15223-1:2016 for CLINICAL THERMOMETER or PROBE with expiration date (Table 201.D.2.101, symbol 2); e) special storage and/or handling instructions; and for a specific MODEL OR TYPE REFERENCE, the indication of single use shall be consistent (No single use applies here).

Instructions for use shall contain: a) summary of USE SPECIFICATION per IEC 62366-1:2015; b) MEASURING SITE and REFERENCE BODY; c) recommended minimum measuring time and minimum time between measurements; d) RATED OUTPUT RANGE for each intended REFERENCE BODY SITE; e) LABORATORY ACCURACY in the RATED OUTPUT RANGE; f) for thermometers with PROBE COVER: instructions for application and behaviour without PROBE COVER (not applicable here - no PROBE COVER used); g) mode of operation (DIRECT MODE or ADJUSTED MODE); h) instructions for selection and replacement of INTERNAL ELECTRICAL POWER SOURCES.

The RISKS of changing environmental conditions for the CLINICAL THERMOMETER shall be considered in the RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS. Guidance regarding the RESIDUAL RISKS shall be provided in the instruction for use (Refer to Operation Guide).

At least one of the following functions shall be identified as ESSENTIAL PERFORMANCE in the RISK MANAGEMENT FILE: accuracy of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER; generation of a TECHNICAL ALARM CONDITION; not providing an OUTPUT TEMPERATURE.

The surfaces of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER, PROBE and ACCESSORIES that can become contaminated with body fluids during NORMAL CONDITION or SINGLE FAULT CONDITION shall be designed to allow for cleaning and disinfection or cleaning and sterilization. The CLINICAL THERMOMETER and PROBE ENCLOSURES shall be designed to allow for surface cleaning and disinfection to reduce to acceptable levels the RISK of infection of OPERATORS, bystanders, or the PATIENT. Instructions for processing and REPROCESSING shall comply with ISO 17664:2004 and ISO 14937:2009 and shall be disclosed in the instructions for use.

Check compliance by inspection of the RISK MANAGEMENT FILE. When compliance with this document could be affected by the cleaning or the disinfecting of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER, PROBE or its parts or ACCESSORIES, clean and disinfect them 100 times in accordance with the methods indicated in the instruction for use, including any cooling or drying period. After these PROCEDURES, confirm that BASIC SAFETY and ESSENTIAL PERFORMANCE are maintained. Confirm that the MANUFACTURER has evaluated the effects of multiple PROCESS cycles and the effectiveness of those cycles.

If the INTENDED USE of a CLINICAL THERMOMETER, PROBE, its parts or ACCESSORIES includes treatment of children or treatment of pregnant or nursing women, a specific justification for the use of phthalates shall be included in the RISK MANAGEMENT FILE. The instructions for use shall contain information on RESIDUAL RISKS for these PATIENT groups and, if applicable, on appropriate precautionary measures. The ACCESSIBLE PARTS that contain phthalates classified as carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic to reproduction shall be marked as containing phthalates on the device itself or on the packaging.

If the CLINICAL THERMOMETER cannot indicate a temperature within the LABORATORY ACCURACY, it either provides a TECHNICAL ALARM CONDITION, or it does not provide an OUTPUT TEMPERATURE. Minimum RATED OUTPUT RANGE of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER is from 34°C to 42°C. Actual rated output range: 32.0°C to 42.9°C.

CLINICAL THERMOMETERS intended for home healthcare use require the display of OUTPUT TEMPERATURE of at least 4mm or the value is optically magnified to this height. This is indicated in USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS. Actual display height: 10mm. CLINICAL THERMOMETERS with a segmented indication display perform a functional test of all segments after activation (N/A for this device).

LABORATORY ACCURACY requirements: Within the RATED OUTPUT RANGE in NORMAL USE shall be within ±0.3°C. Within the RATED EXTENDED OUTPUT RANGE in NORMAL USE shall be within ±0.4°C unless CLINICAL THERMOMETER indicates that the measured temperature is outside of the RATED OUTPUT RANGE. Actual result: 0.3°C for both ranges. If the PROBE is separable from the CLINICAL THERMOMETER, they may be tested separately (N/A). Calculated equation for CLINICAL THERMOMETER: See Appended Table 201.101.2.

Time response for continuous CLINICAL THERMOMETER: The transient response for a DIRECT MODE CLINICAL THERMOMETER that is not an ADJUSTED MODE CLINICAL THERMOMETER shall be characterized and disclosed in the instructions for use. Result: Not a DIRECT MODE CLINICAL THERMOMETER. Transient time lower than recommended minimum measuring time indicated in ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENT (N/A).

CLINICAL ACCURACY VALIDATION (201.102, N/E): ADJUSTED MODE CLINICAL THERMOMETERS are VALIDATED for CLINICAL ACCURACY in each ADJUSTED MODE in accordance with ISO 14155-1:2003 and ISO 14155-2:2003. Results disclosed in ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENT. New PROBE COVER used for each OUTPUT TEMPERATURE measurement if intended for use with PROBE COVER. Human subject population: total febrile subjects 30%-50% of all subjects. Validation carried out on all age groups indicated in instructions for use. Minimum subjects: overall 105, per age group 35, minimum 15 in A1 or A2 if subgroup A is not excluded. Age groups: A1 (0-3 months), A2 (3-12 months), B (>1 and <5 years), C (>5 years).
Electromagnetic compatibility (201.17): IEC 60601-1:2005 Clause 17 applies. Not evaluated in this report (N/E).
ME SYSTEMS (201.16): IEC 60601-1:2005+A1:2012 Clause 16 applies. Result: Not ME systems (N/A).

Substances carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic to reproduction: Check compliance by inspection of the instructions for use and inspection of the information provided by the MANUFACTURER for identification of the presence of such substances and justification for their use. Status: N/E.
An ADJUSTED MODE CLINICAL THERMOMETER that makes continuous estimates of the REFERENCE BODY SITE temperature is exempt from the requirements of this subclause.

IEC 60601-1-2:2014 applies except as follows for section 202 Electromagnetic disturbances. Amendment to 202.4.3.1: add after the last dash of 4.3.1 -- if applicable, attachment of ACCESSORIES as necessary to achieve the BASIC SAFETY and ESSENTIAL PERFORMANCE of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER. Amendment to 202.5.2.2.1: add note to list element b: NOTE: the requirements of this document are not considered deviations or allowances.

The CLINICAL THERMOMETER may exhibit temporary degradation of performance (e.g. deviation from the performance indicated in the instructions for use during IMMUNITY testing), which does not require OPERATOR intervention and that does not affect BASIC SAFETY or ESSENTIAL PERFORMANCE. In the event of disruption during IMMUNITY tests, the CLINICAL THERMOMETER shall recover from any disruption within 30 s.

For usability (clause 206), IEC 60601-1-6:2010+A1:2013 applies. For a CLINICAL THERMOMETER, PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTIONS include: observing the OUTPUT TEMPERATURE; properly positioning CLINICAL THERMOMETER or PROBE at the MEASURING SITE; starting the CLINICAL THERMOMETER from power off; turning off the CLINICAL THERMOMETER; performing a basic pre-use functional check of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER. If available, additional PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTIONS include: performing a basic pre-use functional check of the ALARM SIGNALS; configuring the ACCESSORIES including connection of the detachable parts; REPROCESSING the ACCESSORIES; setting OPERATOR-adjustable controls (switching between MEASURING SITES, setting CLINICAL THERMOMETER control parameters, setting ALARM LIMITS, inactivating ALARM SIGNALS).
Clause 208.6.1.2 Amendment: A CLINICAL THERMOMETER need not have a PHYSIOLOGICAL ALARM CONDITION. This is an amendment added prior to the compliance check for IEC 60601-1-8:2006+A1:2012.

Clause 211.10.1.1: The tests of IEC 60601-1-11:2015, Clause 10 and IEC 60601-1:2005+A1:2012, 15.3 shall be performed on the same sample of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER after the cleaning and disinfection PROCEDURES. This requirement applies to the home healthcare environment.

Clause 212.10.1.1 Amendment: The tests of IEC 60601-1-12:2014, Clause 10 and IEC 60601-1:2005+A1:2012, 15.3 shall be performed on the same sample of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER after the cleaning and disinfection PROCEDURES of 201.11.6.6 of this document have been performed unless there are no cleaning and disinfection PROCEDURES specified in the instructions for use. If more than one PROCEDURE is specified in the instructions for use, each PROCEDURE shall be so tested. A separate sample of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER [text truncated]. This requirement applies to the emergency medical services environment.

Laboratory accuracy test data (201.101.2): The clinical thermometer was tested at three temperature points (midpoint 37.0°C, upper limit 42.0°C, lower limit 33.0°C) of the rated output range (32.0°C to 42.9°C) under five combinations of ambient conditions (25°C/55%RH, 39.5°C/90%RH, 10.5°C/90%RH, 39.5°C/20%RH, 10.5°C/20%RH). All equation values (deviations) were within ±0.2°C. The RATED EXTENDED OUTPUT RANGE is N/A for this device.

Combination of upper and lower limits of environmental temperature and humidity ranges for testing: 1) Midpoint of humidity and ambient temperature; 2) Upper limit of humidity + upper limit of ambient temperature; 3) Upper limit of humidity + lower limit of ambient temperature; 4) Lower limit of humidity + upper limit of ambient temperature; 5) Lower limit of humidity + lower limit of ambient temperature.

Temperature measurement abbreviations used in the report: TRTS – Measured temperature of REFERENCE TEMPERATURE SOURCE; TTUT – Measured temperature of CLINICAL THERMOMETER under test; TRCT – Measured temperature of REFERENCE CLINICAL THERMOMETER. Note: reference temperature source and reference clinical thermometer are same one thermometer.

Alarm and output behavior requirement (Clause 201.12.1.101): When the CLINICAL THERMOMETER is not capable of indicating a temperature within the LABORATORY ACCURACY, it shall provide a TECHNICAL ALARM CONDITION or it shall not provide an OUTPUT TEMPERATURE. Verified behavior: (1) Shows 'LOW POWER REMINDER' symbol when low voltage of the internal electrical power source; (2) Shows '- - -°F' or '- - -℃' when output temperature is outside the rated extended output range.

It is the responsibility of the MANUFACTURER of a PROBE, PROBE CABLE EXTENDER and PROBE COVER, including a REPROCESSED PROBE, PROBE CABLE EXTENDER and PROBE COVER, to have their PROCESSES VALIDATED to ensure that any new or REPROCESSED product complies with the requirements of this particular standard

The following degradations, if associated with BASIC SAFETY or ESSENTIAL PERFORMANCE, shall not be allowed: component failures; changes in programmable parameters or settings; reset to default settings; change of operating mode; change in LABORATORY ACCURACY greater than permitted in 201.101.2 without generating a TECHNICAL ALARM CONDITION or indication of abnormal operation
